flag.name: Flag of Connecticut
flag.description: Azure blue, charged with an argent white shield of rococo design, having in the center three grape vinces, supported and bearing fruit in natural colors. THe bordure to the shield is gold on the interior and silver on the exterior, adorned with natural-colored clusters of white oak leaves bearing acorns. Below the shield is a white streamer, cleft on each end, bordered by a band of gold within fine brown lines, and upon the streamer in dark blue block letters is the motto "QUI TRANSTULIT SUSTINET".
flag.symbolism: The design comes from the seal of Saybrook Colony. The three grapevines represent the three oldest settlements of Windsor, Wethersfield, and Hartford, or the three settlements of Connecticut Colony, Saybrook Colony, and New Haven Colony. The grapes themselves represent providence and faith. The leaves and acorns represent antiquity. The banner has the motto of Connecticut, meaning "He who transplated sustains," which connects to the symbolism of the grape vines.

seal.name: Great Seal of the State of Connecticut
seal.description: Three grape vines, supported and bearing fruit in natural colors. Below, a blue streamer, cleft on each end, reading "QUI TRANSTULIT SUSTINET." On the border of the seal is written "SIGILLUM REIPUBLICÆ CONNECTICUTENSIS."
seal.symbolism: The design comes from the seal of Saybrook Colony.
